q: Formulate the assignment model and state its relation to the transportation model.
a: Let xij = 1 if facility i is assigned to job j and 0 otherwise. Minimize Z = sum cij xij subject to sum over j of xij = 1 for every i, sum over i of xij = 1 for every j. Replacing xij in {0,1} by xij >= 0 gives a transportation model in which all supplies and demands equal 1.

q: State the steps of the Hungarian method.
a: Balance the matrix; subtract each row's minimum; subtract each column's minimum; assign zeros (circle a lone zero and cross out other zeros in its row/column); if each row and column has one circled zero it is optimal; otherwise cover all zeros with the minimum number of lines, subtract the smallest uncovered element from uncovered elements and add it at intersections, and repeat.
Row minima 15, 12, 21, 17, 16, then column minima 0, 0, 0, 2, 3 give a zero matrix with a complete assignment: 1-II (15), 2-IV (14), 3-I (21), 4-V (20), 5-III (16) for a total of 86 hours.

q: How are maximization and unbalanced assignment problems handled?
a: Maximization: subtract every element from the largest element (e.g. 42) and solve as a minimization (answer 99 for the 4x4 example). Unbalanced: add dummy rows or columns with zero cost to make the matrix square (the 5x4 example adds a dummy job and gives total cost 54).
